title: Three new directions for iyyam
question: Choose the visual world you want developed. These are illustrative first-screen sketches; the live app is unchanged.

options.label: Daylight
options.thesis: A porcelain desk clock with crisp ink-blue numerals and softly raised controls.
options.lineage: Porcelain domestic objects and clear printed calendars
options.viewport: Local time anchors a porcelain inset; a wider quiet waqt field sits beside it, with dates and calendars below.
options.risk: A light surface needs careful dimming for nighttime use.

options.label: Nocturne
options.thesis: A low-light clock with pearl digits, aubergine depth and amber prayer boundaries.
options.lineage: Evening interiors, dyed textiles and bedside lighting
options.viewport: A centered luminous clock leads the upper field; a wider horizontal waqt band and compressed date rail sit below.
options.risk: Quiet secondary text must still be readable across the room.

options.label: Meridian
options.thesis: A mineral-teal daily clock with the prayer day made legible as one continuous timeline.
options.lineage: Shared daily rhythms and disciplined civic wayfinding
options.viewport: The largest local digits face a wider waqt field; a continuous prayer timeline joins the day before the three-calendar area.
options.risk: The timeline must remain supporting information, without competing with the clock.
